inputs.share_count_basis: ADS basis. Q2-2026 diluted weighted average 2,755m Class A+B ordinary shares / 8 ordinary shares per ADS = 344.4m ADS (basic 2,716m = 339.5m ADS). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the US$5.0bn buyback (US$259m spent 2026 YTD at the Q2 release) is the funding mechanism, not an extra source of value.
inputs.ads_note: 1 ADS = 8 Class A ordinary shares. shares_outstanding, every intrinsic_value and current_price are per ADS (the Nasdaq BIDU unit). Per ordinary share (9888.HK) = per-ADS value / 8, converted USD->HKD.
inputs.net_debt_note: Baidu excluding iQIYI, RMB m, 30 June 2026. Cash = cash 24,524 + restricted 170 + short-term investments 141,727 + long-term time deposits and held-to-maturity 74,311 = 240,732 consolidated, less iQIYI cash and restricted cash 3,206 (Q2-2026 segment cash flow table) and an ESTIMATED 1,000 of iQIYI short-term investments. Debt = short-term loans 26,311 + long-term loans 2,027 + 20,779 + notes payable 2,038 + 46,089 + convertible notes 1 + 6,615 = 103,860 consolidated, less iQIYI indebtedness 14,800 (latest disclosed figure, 31 Dec 2025, FY2025 20-F risk factor). Operating lease liabilities (9,037) are excluded: US GAAP operating lease cost is already inside adjusted EBITDA.
inputs.sbc_source: Q4-2025 6-K non-GAAP reconciliation, Baidu General Business share-based compensation FY2025 (consolidated 3,605 incl. iQIYI 402). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed in the cash flow statement, so nothing is added on top. H1-2026 Baidu General Business SBC ran 1,122 (2.2% of revenue), which anchors the forward path.
inputs.fcf_note: reported_fcf is Baidu excl. iQIYI FY2025 (OCF -3,119 less capex 11,978). OCF was negative because 22.4bn flowed out through 'other assets', chiefly long-term advances to suppliers (8.9bn -> 18.0bn) -- prepaid compute hardware that is capex in substance. interest_income is the consolidated FY2025 figure (iQIYI's share is not split out and is small). The forward build starts from adjusted EBITDA, so interest income never enters the flows.
inputs.fx_note: USD/CNY 6.6712 (Yahoo CNY=X, 2026-11-14) -> 0.1499 USD per CNY, model -> quote. Direction check via the dual-primary listing: 9888.HK HK$74.2 (2026-11-12 close) x 8 ordinary per ADS / USD/HKD 7.8455 = US$75.66 per ADS, within about 3% of the Nasdaq ADS close one session later. The Q2-2026 release translated at 6.7851 (30 June 2026 H.10).
inputs.wacc_rationale: 10% on CNY flows, the same in every scenario. A CNY-built CAPM (China 10-year about 2%, mature ERP plus China country premium about 6.5-7%, beta about 1.0) gives roughly 8.5-9%; the extra 1-1.5pp is the single charge for risks the scenario flows do not carry -- the VIE structure, HFCAA/PCAOB contingency, and trapped onshore cash. Operating risk (search decline, GPU export controls, cloud returns) lives in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate. Terminal growth 2.0-3.0% reflects low CNY inflation.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) by construction: US GAAP operating lease cost sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside adjusted EBITDA; lease liabilities (RMB 9.0bn) are excluded from net debt. lease_cost_pct_path left at zero so the lease is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: iQIYI is DECONSOLIDATED rather than run through an NCI leakage rate: flows are Baidu General Business only, iQIYI's debt and cash are removed from net debt, and Baidu's roughly 45% economic stake is added back at market value in the equity bridge. Remaining minorities are deducted once, in the bridge, at book: redeemable NCI ex-iQIYI (subsidiary preferred shares) and an estimated non-iQIYI ordinary NCI.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) on Baidu General Business, plus a sum-of-parts bridge for iQIYI, long-term investments and minorities. Reason: Baidu is an operating company, but consolidated FCF includes 100% of iQIYI, which Baidu only about 45% owns, which is roughly break-even, and which carries RMB 14.8bn of its own debt; valuing the stake at market and stripping the segment is cleaner than a leakage rate and the releases publish the full segment split (revenue, adjusted EBITDA, SBC, D&A, OCF, capex). FY0 = FY2025 Baidu General Business revenue. FY2026 is the first forecast year and is three quarters elapsed: H1-2026 actual free cash flow excl. iQIYI (-11,629) has already left the 30 June balance sheet and is added back in the bridge so it is not charged twice. No Q3-2026 release was in the folder at the valuation date; it should be the first refresh. Capex path deliberately includes compute prepayments that the company books through operating cash flow. Buybacks are funded (repurchaser), so the flat count is real. The first-ever dividend and the Kunlunxin spin-off are not modelled as value: the dividend is a distribution of cash already in the bridge, and Kunlunxin's flows are inside Baidu General Business -- the reported US$50bn target valuation is unconfirmed and is discussed as upside in the bull narrative only. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

Equity-method earnings sit below operating income and are not in the flows.

equity_bridge.note: ESTIMATE: total NCI 9,660 less iQIYI minorities of roughly 7,400 (about 55% of iQIYI net assets). Not separately disclosed in the releases.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: segment_build (base-case 10-year Baidu General Business revenue CAGR)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (7.9%) is more than 30% above the revenue 5-year CAGR (3.8%) and net income shrank; equity grew on retained investment gains and interest, not operations, so it is NOT used as the growth anchor. Growth is built from the segment mix instead.
historical_growth.notes: Consolidated series, FY2020/FY2022 -> FY2025. EPS is not populated in the CSV, so the EPS rows use net income (FY2020 22,472, FY2022 7,559, FY2025 5,589; FY2025 carries a 16.2bn impairment). Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income) was 7,030 in FY2020, 4,851 in FY2022 and -27,293 in FY2025: a CAGR is undefined across a sign change. Reported FCF fell from 19,116 to -15,086 over the same span while SBC fell from 6,728 to 3,605, so the deterioration is capex and compute prepayments, not stock comp.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026: H1 Baidu General Business revenue 51,184 vs 51,714 (-1%), with easier H2 comparisons. Thereafter a segment build: legacy search declining 17% -> 8% a year from about 41bn, AI Cloud Infra growing 35% -> 10% from about 31bn, AI Applications and AI-native marketing high single to low double digits.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC) for Baidu General Business was 29.2% in FY2024, 21.5% in FY2025 and 23.8% in H1-2026. The mix shift from search (40%+ margin) to cloud holds the margin flat until GPU cloud scales, then lifts it to 28% -- below the FY2024 level.
base.capex_rationale: H1-2026 capex excl. iQIYI was 17.2bn (33.6% of revenue; Q2 alone 11.4bn) and FY2025 added roughly 9bn of long-term supplier advances through operating cash flow. 38% in FY2026 covers both; intensity then glides to 16% against D&A of 15%, a steady state for a business half of whose revenue is cloud infrastructure. D&A is understated today because the FY2025 16.2bn impairment cut the depreciable base.

scenario_narratives.base: The replacement works, at lower returns. Legacy search and feed advertising keeps shrinking (17% a year easing to 8%) as AI answers displace paid clicks, but AI Cloud Infra compounds from about 31bn at 35% easing to 10%, and AI-native marketing recovers part of the lost ad yield. Baidu General Business revenue is flat in FY2026 and grows about 5.4% a year over the decade. Margins never return to the search era: adjusted EBITDA recovers from 23.5% to 28% (FY2024 was 29%), and the business becomes structurally capital-intensive, with capex settling at 16% of revenue against 11.7% in FY2025. Owner FCF is negative through FY2027 and matures near 8% of revenue. Apollo Go is carried at its current cost inside the margin with no separate payoff.
scenario_narratives.bull: GPU cloud demand outruns supply constraints because Kunlunxin chips substitute for restricted Nvidia parts, so AI Cloud Infra sustains 40%+ growth for three years and reaches scale margins; AI-native marketing monetises AI answers at close to the legacy rate, slowing the ad decline; Apollo Go's asset-light partnerships (Uber, Lyft) turn the robotaxi unit from a cost into a contributor. Revenue grows about 7.6% a year and adjusted EBITDA reaches 32%. This needs three independent things to go right. A Kunlunxin listing at anything like the reported US$50bn would be further upside not in these flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: The pivot substitutes revenue but not profit. Search advertising falls faster than AI lines replace it for two more years; tighter US export controls cap GPU capacity so cloud growth stalls in the teens while price competition with Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance holds cloud margins down; the compute already bought earns a poor return. Revenue shrinks through FY2027 and then grows about 3%; adjusted EBITDA sinks to 19.5-20.5% and owner FCF matures near 3% of revenue. In this path the operations are worth little and the equity is a discounted claim on the balance sheet -- which is roughly what the current price implies.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the house 15% to 25%: the thesis rests on a pivot whose economics are unproven -- owner FCF is currently negative, the fastest-growing segment depends on GPU supply a single regulator can restrict, and the legacy decline is still accelerating. Base held at 50%: it follows the reported segment trajectory and assumes margins below FY2024. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs chip substitution, ad re-monetisation and robotaxi economics to all work.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Baidu is valued as two things: an operating business in a capital-intensive transition (Baidu General Business, owner-FCF DCF in CNY at 10%), and a balance sheet (net cash and deposits ex-iQIYI of about RMB 147bn, long-term investments at 80% of adjusted value, the iQIYI stake at market, minorities deducted at book). The non-operating bridge alone comes to about RMB 179.5bn -- essentially the whole market capitalisation at the valuation-date price -- so the market is paying roughly nothing for the operations. The valuation therefore turns on two questions the model answers conservatively: whether the operations are worth more than zero after the compute build-out, and how much of the cash a Nasdaq/HK holder can actually reach.
key_risks_to_valuation: Balance-sheet value dominates: about three quarters or more of base equity value is cash, deposits and investments, most of it held onshore in PRC subsidiaries and VIEs. Repatriation carries 5-10% withholding tax and needs regulatory clearance; none of that is deducted beyond the 10% discount rate.
Capex and compute prepayments: FY2026 investment is running near 35-40% of segment revenue. If intensity stays above 20% rather than gliding to 16%, base operating value goes to about zero.
Debt rose RMB 14bn in H1-2026 while cash was being accumulated in deposits -- gross balances are large on both sides and the net position should be re-read from every release.

iQIYI deconsolidation rests on two estimates (iQIYI short-term investments, non-iQIYI NCI) and a 31 Dec 2025 iQIYI debt figure; Baidu's notes carry cross-default provisions with iQIYI, so the 14.8bn is not perfectly ring-fenced.
Long-term investments are haircut 20% by judgment; a full write-down would cost about US$15 per ADS.
FY2025 D&A is flattered by the 16.2bn impairment; reported operating margins overstate steady-state profitability until depreciation catches up with the new asset base.
FX: value is built in CNY and quoted in USD at a spot rate that refresh_price does not update.
